subject: URGENT: SparkRx production impact — AZ3 throughput collapse & geo-swap request
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sparkrx.com>

Cc: SparkRx Platform Ops <ops@sparkrx.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Jul 2029 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: P0: sudden throughput collapse in us-west-2 AZ3 — immediate help needed

Mina / Redwood on-call,

We're seeing a hard drop in throughput and a spike in 502/504 errors for our production traffic routed to us-west-2 AZ3. Impact started ~14:45 PDT and has persisted for the last 25 minutes — customer-facing latency is up to 6s and overall QPS is down ~80%. High-level:

- Error types: 502 / 504 / connection timeouts
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (main route), some chat endpoints
- Region: us-west-2, primarily AZ3 (per our tracing)
- Business impact: several merchant checkouts failing; Page load errors reported across many users

We've attached a short capture and server-side logs (error_logs_20290707.zip). We urgently need Redwood to:

1) confirm root cause (if visible)
2) provide immediate mitigation — warm traffic to another region or fail over if necessary
3) timeline and expected recovery steps

This is blocking our high-volume customers and our CS/ops team have already escalated internally. Please advise next steps and whether you need anything else from our side (additional logs, API keys, etc.).

Thanks – Alex
Alex Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, SparkRx
[Attachment: error_logs_20290707.zip (log bundle, 3.1 MB)]

Alex — thanks for the quick heads-up and for attaching the logs. We're triaging now.

High-level plan (immediate):
- Triage: Jonas (SRE) is pulling KV and routing metrics — initial suspicion is cache/KV saturation combined with an AZ-local network jitter causing connection resets.
- Short-term mitigation: If AZ-level drain is required we'll propose a controlled geo-swap to us-west-1 with a gradual canary (to avoid cold-start spike). This requires an exec-level authorization for emergency geo-swap and a short maintenance window.
- Data/impact: please confirm whether SparkRx has any hard affinity (IP whitelists, regional IP allowlist) that would block traffic from us-west-1. Also, if you have any stateful coupling (session pins) we need to know.

Jonas — any early findings you can paste here? Hannah — can you standby to coordinate a drain and adjust routing at the edge if we go ahead?

I'll loop in Rishi for commercial/credits discussion (Rishi, heads-up — SparkRx is requesting both remediation and clarification on compensation).

Subject: Re: P0: sudden throughput collapse in us-west-2 AZ3 — immediate help needed

Quick technical summary from initial probes: 

- Observations:
  - AZ3 shows sustained high socket reset rates and elevated KV cache miss rate ~65% (normal ~8-12%).
  - Per-instance CPU is fine; latency tails increase when cache miss + network retries combine.
  - Error spike correlates with a set of customer routes that send large prefixes; KV growth pattern suggests a small set of keys are thrashing the cache and driving eviction storms.

- Immediate mitigations (recommended order):
  1) Short-term: divert new sessions away from AZ3 (gradual drain) -> route to us-west-1 as canary (5% -> 25% -> 100% if healthy).
  2) Apply dynamic prefix bypass for hot prefixes (reduce KV pressure while warm caches populate in us-west-1).
  3) Limit per-route concurrency for /v1/generate for SparkRx customer token to prevent amplification.
  4) If needed, fallback to a lighter-weight quantized model in us-west-1 to absorb burst QPS while recovery completes.

I attached a KV snapshot and a short trace (kvstats_snapshot.txt, handshake_trace.pcap) — size is small. If we proceed with a geo-swap we should:
- schedule a 10 minute canary and monitor latency, error-rate, and token cost;
- warm top-n prefixes in us-west-1 before moving traffic settings to avoid cold-cache spike.

I'll stand by to perform the drain and routing changes once we have exec approval.

Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: P0: sudden throughput collapse in us-west-2 AZ3 — controlled geo-swap completed

Alex / SparkRx team — thank you for your patience. Final update and post-action notes:

What we did:
- At 2029-07-08T23:20:00Z we executed a controlled geo-swap to us-west-1 following the approved canary plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Warmed top 200 prefixes in us-west-1 before moving the bulk of traffic; applied dynamic prefix bypass for known hot keys.
- Enforced a temporary per-route concurrency cap for /v1/generate on SparkRx tokens to avoid amplification while caches filled.

Immediate results:
- End-to-end P50 latency fell from ~1.6s to 0.34s on the canary and stabilized at 0.45s post-cutover.
- Error rate dropped from 18% to 0.6% within 14 minutes of full cutover.
- Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline within 35 minutes.

Artifacts attached and next steps:
- Attachments: error_logs_20290707.zip, kvstats_snapshot.txt, handshake_trace.pcap (same as triage pack).
- We're continuing to monitor KV eviction patterns; Jonas will follow up with a deeper postmortem and mitigation steps to prevent recurrence (likely cache policy changes or hot-key sharding).
- Rishi — please confirm the agreed credit and I'll include the commercial note in the postmortem.
- We'll publish a short customer-facing incident summary and share the internal postmortem within 72 hours.

If anything regresses or you see anomalies on your side, please reopen this thread and ping the on-call channel.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
